name: a live window with no shape of work enabled matches nothing, and says so

steps._step: THE UNMATCHABLE STATE, arrived at by doing nothing. Alice's window is live and she has never said what work she will take, so no role can reach her.

expect._note: matchable is false against a live window. Every flag is false because that is the default (decision 12) — opting somebody into internships by inaction would put them in front of hirers they never agreed to hear from. current_country is empty and office_yoe null: nothing has been stated, and null is not zero. open_source_years is null because this case seeds no claims, and a contributor with no merged evidence has no derived figure rather than a figure of zero. needs_attention is TRUE, and this is the only pairing where both fields say the same thing for the same reason: nobody has asked her, so there is nothing to respect and something to prompt.

steps._step: ONE shape is enough to become findable. Nothing about her availability changed.

user_work_preferences._note: One row, inserted rather than updated: this is the first time she has submitted the form.

steps._step: Carol's window LAPSED yesterday. Same default flags, and the same answer for a different reason.
ALL FOUR FLAGS, and still unmatchable. Decision 5: the flags do not lapse separately, so a dead window takes every one of them down with it.

expect._note: This is the half of the composition rule an implementation forgets: `Matchable()` on the preferences alone is true here, and the answer is still false because IsActive is not. needs_attention is FALSE here while matchable is false — she has answered, and answering is what stops the prompt. Nagging somebody who filled the form in is how a prompt gets dismissed for good.

steps._step: Refreshing the window is the OTHER repair, and her four flags are untouched by it — decision 11: two tables, two lifetimes, and a write to one cannot clear the other.
Bob is not_looking, which is an explicit refusal rather than a window that ran out — ADR-0008 §1a. It has no expiry to report.
Declaring an onsite preference does NOT re-enter him into the pool. not_looking is the one status no flag can override.
Now both halves hold. Note there is no open_to_freelance flag to set — availability_status already carries freelance, and two controls meaning one thing can disagree (decision 6).
A contributor who signed in a minute ago has NO availability row and no preferences row. The profile read must answer for them rather than 404 — everybody starts here.

Two absent rows and one nil availability, answered rather than crashed. This is the seam a service test cannot reach: the repository returns a zero-valued row for a user it has never seen, and the composition rule has to survive a nil window.
The profile belongs to the contributor surface. A hirer has no work preferences to state.
